note: The sensible bot (tools/bot.mjs) on seeds 1-3 for 8 sim hours (two game days: the clock runs six times faster than the sim) from a fresh game. Proposed from the first run on 8 Oct 2026 at 48 game hours and re-proposed on 8 Oct 2026 when sim seconds became real seconds (the clock six times faster than motion): the same money a real minute, but a quicker start and fewer lost, since a peak lasts a sixth of the sim seconds it did while patience and platform caps are in sim seconds; and lost re-proposed on 11 Oct 2026 when trains began boarding through their stop (two doors a car, 0.7 passengers a second each) instead of all at once on arrival: people who reach the platform while a train stands now catch it, so Stockport's queue rarely reaches its cap and lost fell from about 155 to 30 while cash and milestones stayed in range. Re-proposed again on 11 Oct 2026 when stations began as halts (the owner's decision): Stockport's subway, platform 3 and booking hall come before the second unit (0.17 to 0.4 h), so Heaton Chapel comes later (0.4 to 0.72 h) and everything after a little later; stages cost money, so less cash at the end; and peaks bite again (lost 30 to 205), as the second unit arrives later and Stockport's subway brings more people in. Lost re-proposed on 12 Oct 2026 when demand came from door-to-door journey times (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys): each group draws its own time budget and gives up when its wait has used what's left, so the peaks press on Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme too when full trains leave Stockport (205 to about 350, a third of it beyond Stockport); demand is scaled so the milestones stay where they were (Heaton Chapel 0.72 to 0.65 h, Ardwick 5.55 to 5.2 h). Re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when trains began running to a timetable (docs/DESIGN.md, Timetable): the units now keep an even gap instead of running wherever they were added, so waits are what the journeys assume and far fewer give up (lost about 350 to 80, nearly all at Stockport's first morning, before the second unit); stops overrun when a crowded train meets a crowded platform, but by the second morning the bot's line has the room, so its trains run at most half a minute late. The bot also buys the faster timetable once it has £45,000 spare (a player would, rather than sit on the money), which takes about £20,000 off cash at the end on main too; cash at the end re-proposed to 25,000-55,000 for both. New measures: the share of main-line departures within five minutes of the timetable, the worst lateness in minutes, and the longest daytime quiet (06:00-22:00 with nothing bought, 0.7 h on main). Lost re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when the peaks were made to press again (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys and Platforms; the owner asked for pressure at the stations they buy): no grace past the budget, and a wait past the timetabled gap felt at three times riding, with demand 1.9 to 1.95 so the milestones stay where they were; lost about 80 to 200, nearly 40% of it beyond Stockport (a new measure, lost beyond home %, 33-100; 11, 8 and 12% on seeds 1-3 before), most at Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme in the second morning. Platforms now block, but on the bot's line never engage. The owner agrees ranges when the pacing is settled. `ok` is inside the range, `near` within 15% of it, `off` beyond. Lost and lost beyond home % re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when taxi ranks came (docs/DESIGN.md, Taxi ranks): a share of those who give up at a station with a rank take a cab while one's in, counted as by cab rather than lost, so lost falls (about 200 to 140) and more of it is Stockport's first morning, before the bot can afford a rank (beyond home 38 to 28%); lost re-proposed as 120-300 and beyond home as 25-100, and by cab added at 15-60 (about 32). The bot buys a rank once a dozen have given up at a station, so Stockport's comes just after the second unit and Heaton Chapel a little later (0.65 to 0.75 h). Things going wrong came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Things going wrong): failed trains and signal failures from the second sim hour, one or two in 8 sim hours, with replacement buses and a spare unit the bot buys once a train has failed. The milestones held; what moved is where trouble lands, the second morning's peak on seeds 2 and 3, mostly as Stockport's platform fills behind a held train: lost 139 to about 210 (seed 2's two failed trains 300), cash 50,800 to about 40,300, worst late up to 8 minutes, and lost beyond home 28 to 23%, so that range is re-proposed as 15-100. New measures, proposed: failures 0-3 and signal failures 0-3 a run, and lost in trouble (who gave up while something was wrong or in the quarter hour after) 0-200.
